stimuli.text: A solid insulating sphere of radius R = 0.06 m has a total charge Q = +3 nC distributed uniformly throughout its volume.
An initially uncharged 2 µF capacitor, a 110 kΩ resistor, an ideal 14 V battery and an open switch are connected in series. The switch is closed at t = 0.
Students measure the resistance of different lengths of a wire with a diameter of 0.5 mm, using a battery, an ammeter and a voltmeter.

A conducting rod of mass 0.4 kg and length 0.2 m slides without friction on horizontal rails connected by a 6 Ω resistor. A uniform 1 T magnetic field points vertically through the rails. The rod is given an initial speed of 10 m/s and then released.

questions.stem: A 7 µF capacitor is in series with a parallel combination of 8 µF and 11 µF. What is the equivalent capacitance?

options.why: Not all the capacitors are in series.
Not all the capacitors are in parallel.
The series and parallel rules are swapped (they are the reverse of resistors).
Correct. Capacitors add in parallel; reciprocals add in series.

questions.stem: Two point charges of 3 µC and −3 µC are 0.35 m apart. What is the magnitude of the force between them?
A 50 Ω resistor is connected across 95 V. What power does it dissipate?
A flat circular coil of 18 turns and radius 0.18 m carries 17 A. What is the field at its center?

options.why: That is a straight wire's field.

questions.stem: The current in a wire is $$I(t) = 8t^2$$ A. How much charge passes a point from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 4$$ s?
A 0.3 H inductor carries 10 A. How much energy is stored in its magnetic field?
A uniform field of 200 N/C passes through a flat 0.6 m² surface whose normal makes 60° with the field. What is the flux through the surface?

options.why: θ is measured from the normal, so use cos θ.

questions.stem: A 11 µF capacitor is in parallel with a series combination of 8 µF and 8 µF. What is the equivalent capacitance?

options.why: Not all the capacitors are in series.
Correct. Capacitors add in parallel; reciprocals add in series.
The series and parallel rules are swapped (they are the reverse of resistors).
Not all the capacitors are in parallel.

questions.stem: An electron moves at $$9 \times 10^{6}$$ m/s perpendicular to a uniform 0.15 T magnetic field. What is the radius of its path?

options.why: Correct. qvB = mv²/r, so r = mv/(qB).

questions.stem: An electron starts from rest and is accelerated through a potential difference of 1000 V. What is its final speed? ($$m_e = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}$$ kg)
A battery with emf 19 V and internal resistance 0.4 Ω is connected to a 2 Ω resistor. What is the terminal voltage?

options.why: That is the internal voltage drop.
Correct. I = ε/(R + r); V = ε − Ir.
Some voltage is lost across the internal resistance.

questions.stem: Two identical small conducting spheres carry -7 µC and 6 µC. They are touched together and separated. What is the charge on each?

options.why: Add the charges with their signs.
The total is shared between two spheres.
Correct. Identical conductors share the total charge equally.

questions.explanation: Total -1 µC, split equally: -0.5 µC each.

questions.stem: A 18 µF capacitor is charged to 65 V. How much energy does it store?
A solenoid 0.3 m long has 1500 turns and carries 8 A. What is the magnetic field inside it?

options.why: Correct. B = μ₀nI with n = N/L.
That resembles a wire's field; use B = μ₀nI.

questions.stem: A 200-turn coil of area 0.18 m² is perpendicular to a magnetic field that changes by 0.3 T in 0.1 s. What is the magnitude of the average induced emf?

options.why: Multiply by the number of turns.

questions.stem: Two parallel plates 0.09 m apart have a potential difference of 120 V. What is the field between them?

options.why: Correct. In a uniform field, E = ΔV/d.

questions.stem: Point P is 0.2 m from a +1 µC charge and 0.1 m from a −7 µC charge. What is the electric potential at P?

options.why: The negative charge contributes negative potential.
Correct. Potential is a scalar: add kq/r with signs.

questions.stem: A parallel-plate capacitor has plates of area 0.18 m² separated by 2 mm of air. What is its capacitance?
Charges of -4 µC, 3 µC, 1 µC sit at the corners of an equilateral triangle with sides 0.4 m. What is the system's electric potential energy?

options.why: Correct. Add kqᵢqⱼ/r for all three pairs.
Keep the signs of the charges.

questions.stem: A 20 Ω resistor is connected across 85 V. What power does it dissipate?
How much work must an external agent do to move a +8 µC charge slowly from a point at -10 V to a point at 26 V?
A long straight wire carries 6 A. What is the magnetic field 0.19 m from it?

options.why: That is the field at the center of a loop.
A long wire's field falls off as 1/r.

questions.stem: A long straight wire carries a uniform charge of 9 µC/m. What is the field 0.45 m from it?

options.why: A line charge's field falls off as 1/r.
Correct. E = λ/(2πε₀r), from Gauss's law with a cylinder.

questions.stem: A wire 40 m long has a diameter of 2 mm and resistivity $$2.8 \times 10^{-8}$$ Ω·m. What is its resistance?

options.why: Correct. R = ρL/A with A = π(d/2)².

questions.stem: A 0.3 m wire carrying 15 A makes a 60° angle with a uniform 0.6 T magnetic field. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force on it?

options.why: Use sin θ, from the cross product.

questions.stem: A conducting sphere of radius 2 cm carrying 108 nC is connected by a long thin wire to an uncharged conducting sphere of radius 7 cm far away. What charge ends up on the smaller sphere?

options.why: Correct. Connected spheres reach equal potential, so Q ∝ R.
Equal potential gives Q ∝ R, not R².
That is the larger sphere's charge.

questions.explanation: kQ₁/R₁ = kQ₂/R₂ with Q₁ + Q₂ = 108: Q₁ = 24 nC.

questions.stem: A 19 µF capacitor starts uncharged and is charged through a 30 kΩ resistor by a 14 V battery. What is the capacitor's voltage after 1.71 s?

options.why: Convert kΩ and µF to Ω and F.
That is the charging resistor's voltage.
Correct. τ = RC = 0.57 s; V = ε(1 − e^(−t/τ)).
The change is exponential, not linear.

questions.stem: A 4 Ω resistor is in series with a parallel pair of 4 Ω and 3 Ω, connected to an ideal 14 V battery. What is the equivalent resistance?

options.why: Correct. Reduce the parallel pair, add the series resistor, then work back.
R₂ and R₃ are in parallel.

questions.stem: A solid insulating sphere of radius 0.12 m has 3 µC distributed uniformly through its volume. What is the field magnitude 0.204 m from its center?

options.why: Outside, all the charge is enclosed.
Use the distance from the center, r.
Correct. Outside, the sphere acts like a point charge.

questions.stem: A 0.1 m conducting rod slides at 13 m/s along rails connected by a 13 Ω resistor, perpendicular to a uniform 0.1 T field. What is the induced emf?

options.why: Correct. ε = BLv, I = ε/R, F = ILB = B²L²v/R.
That is not the emf; ε = BLv.

questions.stem: A charge of +16q is at $$x = 0$$ and a charge of +q is at $$x = 2$$ m. At what point between them is the electric field zero?

options.why: The zero point is closer to the smaller charge.
Compare r², so take square roots.

questions.stem: A ring of radius 0.23 m carries 4 µC spread uniformly. What is the field magnitude on its axis 0.16 m from the center?

options.why: The charge is not at the center.
Only the axial components add; the others cancel.

questions.stem: Two long parallel wires 0.18 m apart carry 19 A and 12 A in opposite directions. What is the force per meter between them?

options.why: The force per length falls off as 1/d.
Correct. F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd); antiparallel currents repel.
Parallel currents attract; antiparallel currents repel.

questions.stem: A single loop contains a 22 V battery and a 2 V battery connected so their emfs oppose each other, plus resistors of 7 Ω and 4 Ω. What is the current?

options.why: Both resistors are in the loop.
Correct. Loop rule: ε₁ − ε₂ − I(R₁ + R₂) = 0.

questions.stem: Charges of -2 µC, -1 µC, -5 µC sit at the corners of an equilateral triangle with sides 0.1 m. What is the system's electric potential energy?

options.why: Correct. Add kqᵢqⱼ/r for all three pairs.
Keep the signs of the charges.

questions.stem: A parallel-plate capacitor is charged and then disconnected from the battery. A dielectric with κ = 4 is inserted to fill the gap. What happens to the capacitor's stored energy?

options.why: Each quantity changes by at most a factor of κ.
Inserting the dielectric changes the capacitance.
Decide first whether Q or V is held fixed.
Correct. Disconnected, Q is fixed and C rises by κ.

questions.explanation: C becomes κC. Q fixed: V = Q/C and U = Q²/(2C) fall by κ.

questions.stem: Charges of +7 µC and +2 µC are 1 m apart. What is the magnitude of the electric field at the midpoint between them?

options.why: Correct. Like charges' fields point in opposite directions at the midpoint: subtract.
Check the directions of the two fields at the midpoint.
Each charge is d/2 from the midpoint.
The distance is d/2, so r² = d²/4.

questions.explanation: Each field is k q/(d/2)²: 2.52 \times 10^{5} and 7.19 \times 10^{4} N/C, opposite, giving 1.8 \times 10^{5} N/C.

questions.stem: An ideal 16 V battery is connected at $$t = 0$$ to a 5 Ω resistor and a 2 H inductor in series. What is the current at $$t = 0.2$$ s?

options.why: Correct. τ = L/R = 0.4 s; I = (ε/R)(1 − e^(−t/τ)).
The current has not reached its final value.

questions.stem: The electric potential along the x-axis is $$V(x) = 10x^2$$ V. What is the x-component of the electric field at $$x = 1$$ m?

A rectangular loop of length 0.3 m lies in the plane of a long straight wire carrying 3 A, parallel to it. Its near and far sides are 0.05 m and 0.14 m from the wire. What is the magnetic flux through the loop?

options.why: The field is not uniform across the loop.

parts.prompt: Using Gauss's law, derive expressions for the electric field magnitude inside (r < R) and outside (r > R) the sphere.

rubric.criterion: Spherical Gaussian surface; enclosed charge inside is Q(r/R)³.

parts.prompt: Calculate the field magnitude at r = 0.03 m and at r = 0.12 m.
Sketch (describe) a graph of E versus r from 0 to 3R.

rubric.criterion: Linear increase from 0 to a maximum at R, then 1/r² decrease.
rubric.example: Peak value kQ/R² = 7490 N/C at r = R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the electric potential at the surface and at the center (V = 0 at infinity).

rubric.criterion: Center potential by integrating the inside field.

parts.prompt: Write the loop equation for the circuit and solve it to find q(t).
Calculate the time constant, the initial current and the final charge on the capacitor.
Sketch (describe) graphs of the capacitor's voltage and the current versus time.

rubric.criterion: Capacitor voltage rises from 0 toward ε, concave down.
Current decays exponentially from I₀ toward 0.
rubric.example: About 37% of I₀ at t = τ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the energy stored in the capacitor after a long time, and compare it with the energy supplied by the battery.

rubric.criterion: The battery supplies Qε, twice as much; half is dissipated in the resistor.

parts.prompt: Describe (draw) how the ammeter and voltmeter should be connected, and how R is determined.

rubric.criterion: Ammeter in series with the wire; voltmeter in parallel across it.
Keep the current small or brief so the wire does not heat up.

parts.prompt: Plot (describe) R versus L and draw a best-fit line. Calculate its slope.
Use the slope to calculate the resistivity of the wire.

rubric.criterion: Uses slope = ρ/A with A = π(d/2)².

parts.prompt: The students then use a wire of the same material with twice the diameter. Predict the new slope of R versus L and explain.

rubric.criterion: The slope becomes one quarter as large because the area quadruples.

questions.title: A sliding rod in a magnetic field

parts.prompt: Describe qualitatively how the rod's speed changes after it is released, and explain using Lenz's law.

rubric.criterion: The rod slows down, approaching zero.
rubric.example: Its speed decreases ever more slowly.

rubric.criterion: The induced current produces a magnetic force opposing the motion (Lenz's law).
rubric.example: The force opposes the change in flux.

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the magnetic force on the rod in terms of B, L, v and R.

rubric.criterion: Uses ε = BLv and I = ε/R.

parts.prompt: Write and solve a differential equation for v(t).
Calculate the initial current, and explain where the rod's initial kinetic energy ends up.

rubric.criterion: All of the kinetic energy is dissipated as thermal energy in the resistor.
